candidates.name: claude/equalize_boost
candidates.description:
Edit: scale the DIRECT LETTER READOUT (the component of a w2 column that the tied letter rows read through post_ffn_norm and the final norm; a 9-dim subspace) by 0.5 for (a) the 8 letter-specific "leader suppressor" neurons of layer 22's MLP, model.layers.22.feed_forward.w2.weight columns C 1812, D 464, E 7357, F 6492, G 3344, H 397, I 2786, J 3310, and (b) 4 early-letter "booster" neurons: L22 column 2212 (A), L23 columns 1685 (A), 2595 (A), 1439 (B). The rest of each column is unchanged. 24,398 weights differ in bf16.
Mechanism: after head L22.H12 moves the chosen option to the answer position, the L22 MLP suppresses the currently leading letter through one neuron per letter (-3 to -4.6 logits when that letter leads). There is no such neuron for A or B, and A/B have boosters. Total suppression of a leader: A -1.2, B -2.2, C..J -4.1 to -5.6. That asymmetry makes the model over-pick early letters (practice: A..C predicted 249 vs 168 true out of 512). Halving the late-letter suppressors and the A/B boosters equalises it.
Evidence (paired, practice): screen256 DEV +2.34 (SE 1.35), +9/-3; dose-response for the suppressors alone: alpha 0.5 +1.56 (SE 0.95), alpha 0 +1.56 (SE 1.23) with more churn; adding layer 23's suppressors hurt (+1.17, SE 1.41). HOLDOUT 512 (never used for choices): parent 32.62 -> 33.98, +1.37 (SE 1.01), +17/-10. Side effect: the correct letter's log-probability falls (-0.13), because the suppressors also damp overconfidence.

candidates.name: ed_a/ed_a_v1_letterbias12
candidates.description: Removes the answer-letter position prior written by 12 near-constant MLP neurons. Change: for w2 columns (layer,neuron) (20,1000),(22,190),(17,2401),(17,616),(23,1047),(15,4408),(23,4597),(19,6612),(22,1449),(23,1903),(12,6170),(22,2820), project out (in post_ffn_norm-scaled space) the 9-dim subspace spanned by the centered letter readout directions wn*E[A..J] (column -> (I-QQ^T)(pw*col)/pw); strength 1 (full removal). Mechanism: these neurons are ~constant at the answer position (cv<0.6) and write a fixed preference A,B,C,F >> H,I,J (orig bias in centered logits [1.15 1.66 .57 .16 .03 1.27 -.05 -1.14 -2.09 -1.58]); removal flattens it (S: I -2.59 -> -0.34) with no measurable self-repair (direct-logit prediction matched). Smooth dose-response in direct estimate (peak 0.75-1.0). Measured paired gain: DEV S (DEV[512:768], 256 Qs, not used for selection) acc +2.34 +- 1.35, logp_correct +0.190 +- 0.041; HOLDOUT[0:256] acc +1.17 +- 1.61, logp +0.138 +- 0.039. Subset of ed_a_v2, which measured better.

candidates.name: ed_b/ed_b_bias16_a10
candidates.description: alpha = 1.0. Per-neuron direct logit attribution onto the option-letter unembeddings (through final norm) shows a set of late MLP neurons with near-constant activation whose letter push is an ordinal 'early up / late down' profile (largest: L20 n1000, L22 n190, L17 n2401). candidates.name: claude/routers_x1p5
candidates.description:
Edit: scale the outputs of three weak "early router" heads by 1.5: model.layers.14.self_attn.o_proj.weight columns of head 15 (15*128..16*128-1) and head 12 (12*128..13*128-1), and model.layers.20.self_attn.o_proj.weight columns of head 7 (7*128..8*128-1). 786,432 weights.
Mechanism (H5): besides the main answer-routing head L22.H12 (own-choice accuracy .371), these heads write a weak, partly independent vote for an option (own-choice accuracy .26-.28, agreeing with H12 only 31-36%, right on 15-16% of H12's mistakes; direct effect ~0.1 logit). Amplifying them gives the ensemble more say.
Evidence (paired, chosen on DEV): DEV screen256 +1.17 (SE 0.87), DEV screen2 +1.17 (SE 1.30); dose-response x1.5 +1.17, x2 +1.95, x3 +1.95 (log-prob cost grows: -0.15, -0.20, -0.55). HOLDOUT (measured once, never used to choose): 768 questions, about +0.78 (SE ~0.55): HOLDOUT[0:512] +0.59 (SE 0.70) +8/-5, HOLDOUT[512:768] +1.17 (SE 0.87) +4/-1. The correct letter's log-prob falls by ~0.14.

candidates.name: ed_a/ed_a_qprimacy_L22L20
candidates.description:
Removes the option-ordinal ("primacy") query component from the answer-selecting attention layers L22 and L20.
Change: model.layers.22.self_attn.q_proj.weight and model.layers.20.self_attn.q_proj.weight, all 16 heads. For head h: W_h <- W_h - t t^T W_h (alpha = 1), where W_h = rows h*128:(h+1)*128 and t = normalize(q_norm.weight * v1_g). v1_g is PC1 of the slot-mean key vectors (k_norm outputs averaged over the tokens of options A..J, 120 DEV questions) of kv group g = h//4. Rank-1 per head, 2 tensors.
Mechanism: L22 is NoPE-like (q.k on recorded q_norm/k_norm reproduces the attention logits, residual var 0.3%). Option keys carry an ordinal position signal along v1 (slot means A -5.7, B -3.8, ..., J +0.3; split-half r .97). The answer-position query has a near-constant large component along v1 (about 32% of |q|), so every option-reading L22 head prefers early options by about 2.2 nats (A vs I). L20 (RoPE, but v1 sits in low-frequency pairs) has the same mechanism with an A-first preference of about 1 nat. Removing it flattens the letter prior: centred I goes from -2.1 to -0.6.
Evidence (paired edited - parent): DEV S1 (DEV[512:768], 256 q): +1.95 (SE 1.87), logp(correct) +0.186 (SE 0.060). HOLDOUT 512 practice questions (never used for any choice): +0.39 (SE 1.46), 29 w->r / 27 r->w, logp +0.197 (SE 0.055). The log-prob gain is robust, but the accuracy gain is not significant. A becomes under-picked (gold-A accuracy .43 -> .22).

candidates.name: ed_a/ed_a_qprimacy_L22_half
candidates.description:
Half-strength version, L22 only: model.layers.22.self_attn.q_proj.weight, all 16 heads, W_h <- W_h - 0.5 t t^T W_h, where t = normalize(q_norm.weight * v1_g) and v1_g = PC1 of the L22 slot-mean option keys of kv group h//4. This halves the constant query component that makes L22 heads prefer early options (primacy bias A > ... > J of about 2.2 nats). Rank-1 per head.
Evidence (paired): DEV S1 (DEV[512:768], 256 q): +1.95 (SE 1.03), 6 w->r / 1 r->w, logp +0.129 (SE 0.031). HOLDOUT 512: -0.59 (SE 0.98), 11 w->r / 14 r->w, logp(correct) +0.115 (SE 0.026). The logp gain is robust; there is no accuracy gain.

candidates.name: ed_b/ed_b_g2_L12H13_ablate
candidates.description: Change: model.layers.12.self_attn.o_proj.weight columns 1664:1792 (input of head 13 of layer 12) set to 0 (head L12.H13 ablated); 262,144 weights. Mechanism: L12.H13 (sliding-window layer 12) is the strongest attention writer of the option-end correctness belief that L22.H12 later reads through its keys (projection on the correct-minus-incorrect direction: diff .50, SNR .85, alone picks gold 29% vs 31% for the whole stream). Its contribution is 0.83-correlated with the rest of the stream, so it sets the CONFIDENCE of the belief, not which option wins. Dose-response on DEV S1 (256 q): x0 / x1 / x2 give output entropy 1.24 / .99 / .90 and an unchanged gold rank (diff -0.02 +- 0.08 and +0.004 +- 0.06). Measured: DEV S1 acc +1.17 (SE 1.70), dlogp(correct) +0.56 (SE .08); HOLDOUT[0:512] (never used for choosing) acc -0.59 (SE 1.42), 25 wrong->right / 28 right->wrong, dlogp(correct) +0.513 (SE .054). Expect about 0 accuracy change; it is a calibration fix (much less overconfident when wrong), not an accuracy gain.
